clue.text: Oft-repeated song makes a nun irritable

indicators.note: the letters of a nun irritable make, once rearranged, a new phrase, so makes signals the anagram

explanation.surface: A much-sung tune puts a nun in a bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is the anagram signal: the thirteen letters of A NUN IRRITABLE are rearranged. 'Irritable' looks like part of the sentence's sense but is pure fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This patriotic British anthem is sung over and over at events such as the Last Night of the Proms.

clue.text: Obscure pawnbroker turned painter

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker

indicators.note: turned means the painter's letters are read the other way round

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for a painter

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker who changed career and became an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses RA to AR after UNCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is hard to make out, not plain or evident.

clue.text: Is not any faster at splitting points

indicators.note: splitting means at forces its way into the middle of the compass points

parts.note: E and S, east and south, are compass points

explanation.surface: A runner is no quicker when breaking up the points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faster' is someone who fasts, not a quicker runner: one who eats is not fasting. 'splitting' puts AT between E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes food is plainly not abstaining from meals.

clue.text: New cadet or old soldier

indicators.note: new means the letters of cadet or are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Either a fresh cadet or a veteran of the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal on CADET OR. A redcoat was a British soldier of earlier centuries, named for the red tunic.
explanation.definitionFit: British infantry once wore scarlet tunics, so a soldier of former times was called by that uniform.

clue.text: Is likely to fall for the dustmen

explanation.surface: Someone is about to topple over for the sake of the bin men.
explanation.walkthrough: A totter is British slang for a rag-and-bone man or scrap collector, close to a dustman (a refuse collector).
explanation.definitionFit: One who wobbles unsteadily may tumble; and scrap collectors who scavenge refuse are called by this slang name in Britain.

clue.text: It has a point to drive home

definitions.text: It has a point to drive home

parts.words: It has a point to drive home
parts.note: read as an argument making its point, but literally a sharp metal pin hammered fully into wood

explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter hammers this pointed metal spike into timber, driving it right home.

clue.text: Originally a region lived in by our ancestors

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the period, a noun

indicators.note: originally, read as in an original way, tells us the letters of a region are freshly arranged

explanation.surface: A district first settled by forebears long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' seems to mean long ago but is the anagram signal on A REGION.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric people inhabited this period after the Bronze Age, when tools were forged from a newly worked metal.

clue.text: Danger! Tinkers all over the place in these schools!

indicators.note: all over the place means the letters of danger and tinkers are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that menders run riot in the classrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' signals an anagram of DANGER TINKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are nursery classes for small children before primary education.

clue.text: Do such steps take one's breath away?

definitions.text: Do such steps take one's breath away?

parts.words: Do such steps take one's breath away?
parts.note: take one's breath away suggests wonder, but a long spiralling climb literally leaves one panting

explanation.definitionFit: A spiral staircase turning round a central post is exhausting to climb.

clue.text: Spurred on, hearing hostelry is nigh

indicators.note: hearing tells us the phrase is to be heard, not read

parts.note: an inn in sight: a hostelry is an inn, and something sighted is nigh, close at hand

explanation.surface: Encouraged on hearing that a pub is close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' signals a sound-alike: INN SIGHTED, an inn within sight, is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be urged or provoked into action is to be goaded forward.

clue.text: Oil change needed after expedition in N. Africa

definitions.note: a place in North Africa; the definition names where it lies

indicators.note: after places the changed oil behind the expedition

parts.note: a trip is a journey or expedition

indicators.note: change means the letters of oil are altered into another order

explanation.surface: An oil change is needed after a desert expedition in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges OIL to OLI, which goes after TRIP. The definition is loose: the answer is a city in North Africa, Libya's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya's capital city lies on the North African coast.

clue.text: Rode out to become a man of action

indicators.note: out means the letters of rode are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A man rode away to become someone who gets things done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals an anagram of RODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who performs deeds rather than talking is an activist, a person who acts.

clue.text: Being bent, fiddled

explanation.surface: A crooked person with a stoop, cheating the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddled' tempts as cheated, but here it means played a violin: one bows a fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Stooped or curved forward; and played a violin by drawing the stick across its strings.

clue.text: Musicians forbidden to speak

indicators.note: to speak means the word is said out loud

parts.note: something forbidden is banned

explanation.surface: Players are not allowed to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to speak' looks like what is forbidden, but it signals that BANNED is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of instrumentalists playing together is a pop group or ensemble.

clue.text: It's not easily carved by one in a confused state

indicators.note: in a confused state tells us the letters of by one are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something hard to sculpt for a muddled person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a confused state' is the anagram signal on BY ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: This very dense dark hardwood is famously tough to work with a chisel.

clue.text: Booked with prejudice

parts.note: booked suggests a reservation, but the word is booked alongside prejudice in the title of Jane Austen's novel

explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel pairs this vanity with prejudice in its title.

clue.text: Savoury portion, not well cooked

parts.note: meat that is rare is lightly cooked
a bit is a portion

explanation.surface: A tasty helping that is underdone.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse order in the clue; the charade is RARE then BIT. Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast, a British savoury dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit, melted cheese on toast, is served as a savoury course.

clue.text: Desire in one's child to become a doctor

indicators.note: in places the desire inside the child

parts.note: a son is one's child
an urge is a desire

explanation.surface: A parent hopes their son will grow up to be a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts URGE inside SON.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical practitioner operates on patients.

clue.text: Teems, as spring comes in

indicators.note: comes in means the spring goes inside as

parts.note: to bound is to spring or leap

explanation.surface: Life is plentiful when spring arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a leap, BOUND, which 'comes in' AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present in great numbers is to swarm or be plentiful.

clue.text: Transgression produces resentment

explanation.surface: A crime leads to bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach of law is a misdeed; and the feeling of being affronted is umbrage.

clue.text: The peace subsequently includes the French

indicators.note: includes means the French word is held within

parts.note: since can mean subsequently, from then on
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Afterwards the peace takes in the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts LE inside SINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiet, the absence of noise, is the peace kept in a library.

clue.text: A devout leader insists they're cruel

annotationWithheld.why: A devout leader insists they're cruel (7): A + D (devout leader) inside SISTS needs 'insists' to give both the container indicator 'in' and the letters SISTS, one word doing two jobs, and SISTS is no word
annotationWithheld.clue: A devout leader insists they're cruel

clue.text: Fight and squabble caused Robin's death

parts.note: to spar is to fight
a row is a squabble

explanation.surface: A brawl and an argument led to a man named Robin being killed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Who Killed Cock Robin?, the bird that confesses to the killing with its bow and arrow is this one.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme has this little bird admit it shot Cock Robin.

clue.text: Lift most of the secrecy

parts.note: to lift is to steal

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the is dropped

explanation.surface: Raise nearly all of the hidden matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' means pinch, not raise; 'most of' drops E from THE to leave TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting covertly, without being seen, is moving by furtive means.

clue.text: Minor quarrel, but it turns very loud

indicators.note: turns means the word it is read backwards

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A small spat that becomes a shouting match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses IT to TI, followed by FF.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief petty argument is a spat.

clue.text: Shine as a beginner in a new game

indicators.note: in places the beginner inside the rearranged game
new means the letters of game are given a fresh order

parts.note: L, for learner, marks a beginner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Showing promise as a novice at an unfamiliar sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges GAME to GEAM, and 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A glint or glow of light is a brief shining.

clue.text: Lead astray Helen's mother

indicators.note: astray means the letters of lead wander out of place

explanation.surface: Misleading the mother of Helen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' is the anagram signal on LEAD. In Greek myth Helen of Troy was born to the queen seduced by Zeus as a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek myth names this Spartan queen, visited by Zeus as a swan, as mother of Helen of Troy.

clue.text: Beat the unbeatable

explanation.surface: Overcome the invincible.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat someone is to get the better of them; and the top, finest one cannot be bettered.

clue.text: Self-righteous declaration made by black militants

explanation.surface: Sanctimonious statement issued by armed fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as I'M PI, 'I am pious' (pi is slang for sanctimonious); an impi is a Zulu regiment of warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: The words I'm pi announce one's own piety; and a band of Zulu warriors is called this.

clue.text: Girl meets boy carrying eastern cloth

parts.note: Nan is a girl's name

indicators.note: carrying means the boy holds the eastern letter inside

parts.note: Ken is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl meets a boy who is bringing fabric from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts E inside KEN, after NAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff cotton fabric, originally from Nanjing in China, made into trousers.

clue.text: Rose and disconnected speaker

explanation.surface: A flower and someone who talks incoherently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like the verb (got up) but is the climbing flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing variety of flowering shrub; and one who talks at length without coherence.

clue.text: Would a single blow put him out of the ring?

definitions.text: Would a single blow put him out of the ring?

parts.words: Would a single blow put him out of the ring?
parts.note: a knockout punch is suggested, but the boxer in this light division is pictured as so slight a puff of breath would send him flying

explanation.definitionFit: This is a boxing class for light fighters, imagined as light as a plume.
